thread:
elaine: Heads up — saw a spike in fn_call schema_rejects for the /generate route (tool=search). Console shows 3.2% over last 10m. Anyone touch the tool contract?

kevin: I pushed a tiny change to search v2 yesterday (optional `score` field). Shouldn't break anything but maybe our strict validator rejects unknown keys.

joel: Hmm, the runtime enforces `additionalProperties: false` for tool outputs right now. We did that to prevent downstream surprises.

matt: Can you paste an example of the failing payload?

elaine: Sure — from logs: 
```
{"tool":"search","response":{"id":"abc123","title":"foo","score":0.92}}
```
Error: SchemaValidationError: Unexpected property 'score' (path: response.score)

anita: Ugh. This is that contract-ambiguity problem. Some tool teams add telemetry fields and the strict schema causes fn_call to go to fallback. That generates text outputs & higher cost.

kevin: I can revert the change but I think we should make validator more tolerant: either allow extras or drop to partial-accept mode where we extract expected keys and log the rest.

joel: Partial-accept sounds safer. We could emit a telemetry tag `fncall.partial_accept=true` and surface it on console. Right now the dashboard only shows `schema_reject_rate` as a single number, no breakdown for partial vs full rejects.

matt: Operationally, when this happened earlier we saw an uptick in routing fallbacks — router treats `schema_reject` as unrecoverable and routes to text model. That explains higher token usage.

elaine: Proposed short-term fix: 1) relax additionalProperties for tool outputs to true for canary; 2) add telemetry events with `contract_diff` and a hash of extra keys; 3) update console to show top-5 extra-key signatures.

sam: +1. Also we should tag the telemetry with rollout id and quota-tier so we can correlate with dedicated vs hosted. Right now telemetry cardinality explodes — we need sampling (1%) with guaranteed capture for new signatures.

infra-bot: deploy request queued: canary/validator-relax v1 -> staging, initiated by kevin.

kevin: I'll push canary to 10% with `fncall.partial_accept=true` enabled. Will stream logs to #eng-oncall.

joel: Before we do that, a UX note: the rollout page should show the immediate impact metric (tokens/sec & schema_reject_rate) for the canary group inline. Otherwise SREs miss it.

anita: Also we should avoid silently accepting malicious keys. Maybe enforce a whitelist of allowed primitive types and max string length for extras.

matt: Good point. Suggestion: extras allowed but trimmed if length > 1024 and stored only as hashed signature in telemetry.

elaine: Action items: kevin will run canary 10% relax validator (short window), sam to add telemetry sampling + signature hash, joel to add canary metrics to rollout page, anita to draft safe-accept rules. We'll reconvene in 30m.

kevin: starting deploy now. ping me if you see schema_reject_rate change >0.5% on canary.

sam: I'll add a dashboard panel: `fncall: contract drift (canary vs control)` and wire alert: when new signatures >5 in 1h.

joel: Nice. Also file an incident stub if fallback token usage increases >20% so finance gets notified.

elaine: Thanks all. Keeping this thread open for updates.

infra-bot: canary/validator-relax v1 -> staging succeeded (build 8794).

kevin: canary deployed to 10% at 1841002520. watching.

matt: seeing partial_accept telemetry come in — first extra signature: `response.score`. Sampling set to 1% but we got one full capture.

anita: I pushed the safe-accept rules doc to the docs repo (link: https://git.internal/docs/tool-contracts).

elaine: Good progress. If canary looks stable after 20m we'll roll to 50% and update console flags.

kevin: Rolling to 50% now.

sam: Dashboard updated: canary vs control panels live. Early signal: token usage unchanged, schema_reject_rate for canary down from 3.2% -> 0.1%.

joel: Looks like relaxing validator solves the immediate outage. Follow-ups: add per-tool contract drift panel, default partial_accept true but opt-out via tool metadata, and add quota-tagging so we can bill text fallback correctly.

elaine: Filing a follow-up RFC for the longer-term contract strategy. Thanks everyone.
